entertainment.summary: From fresh takes on familiar staples to unexpected game-changers and brands that simply have it , these are the companies and products earning our ultimate stamp of approval
entertainment.body:
From fresh takes on familiar staples to unexpected game-changers and brands that simply have it , these are the companies and products earning our ultimate stamp of approval.

From fresh takes on familiar staples to unexpected game-changers and brands that simply have it , these are the companies and products earning our ultimate stamp of approval

It was a big year for smartphone releases, and amid all of the foldables, one of the most exciting innovations almost flew under the radar. Samsung’s display on the S26 Ultra has a built-in privacy setting that can even be toggled on for specific parts of the screen (such as a pop-up notification from the bank, for example). We got to see the display in action, and it’s as impressive as promised — the screen is legible and bright when looking directly at it but nearly invisible at an angle.

ASUS had a big year of releases, and while a lot of the attention went to the flashy dual-screen models the brand unveiled, their traditional laptop releases were worth paying attention to as well. The Zenbook A16 has a lightweight design without sacrificing screen size, and the dazzling OLED display also features a touchscreen. You get more ports than you typically expect on a modern laptop, including two USB-C ports, a USB-A port, an HDMI port, and an SD card reader. Overall, it’s a powerful laptop that suits a range of use cases.

The Pixel Watch does what few smartwatches have been able to pull off — look like an actual watch. With a domed display, the face doesn’t call attention to the fact that it’s a screen, and the latest Pixel Watch 5 packs in all of the features you need, including health tracking and sleep tracking, plus features you want but hopefully won’t need, like car-crash detection and SOS satellite communications.

Best known for their affordable TVs, TCL has been raising the bar to become one of the best all-around TV brands, with the right combination of innovation, quality, and value. Their SQD mini-LED TVs deliver greater brightness and contrast, with up to 3,000 peak nits for a vibrant display even in bright rooms.

Boox has proven that an e-reader can be more than an e-reader. The brand’s versatile e-ink gadgets run the gamut from phone-sized e-readers to large note-taking tablets. Because they run Android, you can download a versatile suite of apps. Their latest device is the itty-bitty Picco, which is roughly the size of a playing card. With support for ePub and a microSD slot, you can take a variety of file types to read on the go.

entertainment.body:
Breakout reality star Aspyn Ovard made the heartbreaking announcement that her young daughter is battling terminal cancer.

The content creator tearfully discloses the news in the first episode of Hulu’s “Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County,” which premiered Thursday.

“Everything happened just so out of nowhere,” she says in a confessional. “One day she was OK and the next day she wasn’t.”

In the episode, Ovard — who has three daughters and did not specify which one is sick — opens up about the moment she and her ex-husband, Parker Ferris, received the devastating news that every parent dreads.

“At the hospital, we were like, ‘It has to be fine,'” she recalls. “You can’t fathom they’re actually gonna tell you that your baby has cancer, and that it’s terminal and she could be gone in a month.”

The YouTuber, who is now openly in a throuple with a married couple , adds they have been living in fear of losing their daughter for “over three years” now.

While Ovard shares that her daughter recently had “another stable scan” in a later episode, she also says it’s “unusual for a child with this kind of cancer to have this much time,” but does not provide further details on the diagnosis.

Ovard, 30, and Ferris, 31, met in high school. He proposed in 2015 when Ovard was 19 and he was 20.

entertainment.title: Long-time James Bond Producer Barbara Broccoli Named President of U.K.’s National Film and Television School
entertainment.summary: "With the opening of [NFTS'] Cubby Broccoli Building taking place in January, this is especially meaningful. My father believed in the power of filmmaking," Broccoli said.
entertainment.body:
Barbara Broccoli has been appointed president of the U.K.’s National Film and Television School ( NFTS ), and is the first female president in the school’s history.

The prolific producer succeeds Lord David Puttnam, who will take on the honorary role of President Emeritus in recognition of his outstanding contribution to the NFTS and its continued success.

Broccoli is best known for stewarding the James Bond franchise alongside her brother, Michael G. Wilson, after taking the helm from their father, Albert R. “Cubby” Broccoli. The siblings ceded full creative control of the franchise to Amazon MGM Studios in a joint-venture deal last year, with the announcement of Daniel Craig’s successor imminent . Related Stories Movies Gal Gadot Tearfully Warns Against Rising Antisemitism at Simon Wiesenthal Center Gala Movies Nicole Kidman to Receive Honorary Cesar Award From French Film Academy

Broccoli’s NFTS appointment “builds on her longstanding relationship with the NFTS and her commitment to championing emerging filmmaking talent,” said the school. “Her in-depth knowledge of the industry, exceptional creative achievements and passion for developing new voices will be invaluable as the school continues to strengthen its position as a world-leading institution for film, television and games training.”

Her presidency also comes ahead of the opening of The Cubby Broccoli Building at the NFTS’ Beaconsfield campus in January 2027, officially named by Barbara earlier this year in honor of her late father.

“It’s a tremendous honour to become President of the National Film and Television School, following in Lord David Puttnam’s footsteps,” said Broccoli. “Having been involved with the NFTS for many years, I have seen first-hand the extraordinary talent it develops and the vital role it plays in shaping the future of our industry. With the opening of The Cubby Broccoli Building taking place in January, this is especially meaningful. My father believed in the power of filmmaking and in giving talented people the opportunity to succeed.”

Puttnam, an Oscar-winning producer whose credits include Chariots of Fire , The Killing Fields and Midnight Express , said: “I could not be happier than to be handing over the Presidency of the NFTS to my close friend Barbara. To leave the school in such good hands is repaying the last of the many debts I owe to my predecessor Richard Attenborough. My long relationship with the school, and the challenges we’ve faced and overcome, has in many ways defined my career. I’d like to pay a special tribute to those many, many colleagues who have helped make the NFTS the most rewarding journey of my life.”

entertainment.title: Gal Gadot Tearfully Warns Against Rising Antisemitism at Simon Wiesenthal Center Gala

entertainment.body:
“I didn’t expect to get emotional,” Gal Gadot said, pausing as she grew tearful onstage at the Beverly Wilshire on Wednesday evening. “I’m sorry.”

A few seconds before, the Wonder Woman star was smiling, relaying a story to the crowd at the Simon Wiesenthal Center’s Humanitarian Award Dinner about how the evening’s honoree, Skydance co-CEO Ynon Kreiz , 61, had delivered his baby daughter in a car pulled over on a busy London street.

But Gadot, 41, grew somber when the subject turned to the Oct. 7 massacre and the war it incited. Related Stories Movies Nicole Kidman to Receive Honorary Cesar Award From French Film Academy Movies 'Russell Brand: Open Secret' Documentary Set at Netflix

“I’m frightened by how quickly hatred of Jews is spreading — and how openly it is expressed and accepted,” Gadot said. “If people get used to hearing and seeing hatred and looking the other way, then where does it end?”

Before the ceremony, Kreiz told The Hollywood Reporter he agreed with the Ellisons’ response to an Instagram post by Mark Ruffalo criticizing the merger and Israel . The company said the post traded in “antisemitic tropes.”

“I very much agree with what the Ellisons put out,” Kreiz told THR . “Wholeheartedly.”

Pressed on whether he would work with Ruffalo — whose HBO procedural Task now falls under his purview — Kreiz deflected.

Before Gadot took the stage, remarks were delivered by Jeffrey Katzenberg, 75, and David Ellison , 43, who shares stewardship with Kreiz of Skydance.

entertainment.summary: J Balvin, Feid, Trueno, The Sugar Hill Gang, and more artists celebrated the pioneering reggaetón star at the intimate event in Las Vegas.
entertainment.body:
Music stars and industry leaders gathered at the MGM Grand Marquee Ballroom in Las Vegas on Wednesday (Nov. 11) for an evening that honored Daddy Yankee , The Latin Recording Academy’s 2026 Person of the Year.

As tradition holds, the invite-only gala included a dinner and presentation that ran more than three hours, featuring renditions of Daddy Yankee’s repertoire performed by different artists.

“For the first time in history, the Academy honors one of the great pioneers of reggaeton […] Today, we gather to celebrate his career, his music has brought people together—across cultures and generations,” said Manuel Abud, CEO of The Latin Recording Academy, ahead of welcoming the Puerto Rican artist. “Tonight will be a very special journey through your musical career. We have surprises, first-time moments, and music that we believe inspired you.”

The tribute began with a brief introduction by Jorge Drexler and DJ Playero spinning some of Yankee’s earlier hits, before officially starting with a performance by Anthony Ramos singing “Coraza Divina” (2007) in salsa. Immediately after, Tito El Bambino, Jowell y Randy, and Feid gave a euphoric performance of “Gasolina.”

“To me, he is like an older brother,” Tito told the audience of how he was 12 years old when he met Yankee. “He had vision and believed in the new generations. I pray that God grants this gentleman a long life. Thank you for everything you have done for the entire industry.”

One of the most notable moments of the night was when ’80s hip-hop group The Sugar Hill Gang — whom Yankee is a fan of — brought their “Rapper’s Delight” to the stage. In another special moment, the new generation of rappers, J Noa, Paulo Londra, Trueno, Feid, and Ryan Castro, joined forces on a powerful medley that included “Rompe,” “Gangsta Zone,” “Talento de Barrio,” and “Somos de Calle.”

Other artists who formed part of the special ceremony included Reik and Luisa Sonza doing a bossanova version of “Ella Me Levantó”; Farruko, Rawayana, and Kapo performing a reggae version of “La Despedida”; Natalia Jimenez and Pablo Alborán crooning the crowd with a ballad version of “De Vuelta Pa’ La Vuelta;” Tito Nieves, Oscar D’ Leon, and Nathy Peluso giving “Despacito” a salsa twist; and Pedro Capo and Elena Rose’s classical “Ora Por Mi,” to name a few.

entertainment.title: Nicole Kidman to Receive Honorary Cesar Award From French Film Academy
entertainment.summary: The French Academy paid tribute to the 'Moulin Rouge!,' 'Eyes Wide Shut' and 'Practical Magic' actress, saying Kidman "has never allowed her status as a star to dictate her artistic choices."
entertainment.body:
Nicole Kidman will receive an honorary César, the highest award in French cinema, from the French film academy, the Académie des Arts et Techniques du Cinéma.

The Oscar-winning actress will be honored for her life’s work at the 2027 César awards in Paris in February.

Announcing the honor on Thursday, the Académie called Kidman both “a Hollywood star and a major figure in auteur cinema,” saying the Australian actress “has built a career that defies categorization.” Related Stories Movies 'Russell Brand: Open Secret' Documentary Set at Netflix Movies Golshifteh Farahani Is a Widow Fighting the Exploitation of Kids as the Taliban Nears Kabul in 'When She Hears the Bells' (Exclusive Clip and Chat)

Kidman is among a handful of actors who have achieved success both with studio blockbusters, in films such as Aquaman and Pratical Magic , and with art-house features, in her work with the likes of Stanley Kubrick ( Eyes Wide Shut ), Jane Campion ( The Portrait of a Lady ), Lars von Trier ( Dogville ), and Baz Luhrmann ( Moulin Rouge! ). A five-time Oscar nominee, she won the Academy Award for Best Actress in 2003 for her portrayal of Virginia Woolf in Stephen Daldry’s The Hours . More recently, Kidman received the Volpi Cup for Best Actress at the 2024 Venice Film Festival for her role in Halina Reijn’s Babygirl .

Also a producer, Kidman, through her Blossom Films shingle, has produced, and starred in, such series as Big Little Lies , The Undoing , and Nine Perfect Strangers .

With the honorary César, the French Academy said it wishes “to pay tribute to an actress and producer who has never allowed her status as a star to dictate her artistic choices.”

In recent years, the Césars have singled out Hollywood talent for their honorary award. Last year’s honoree was Jim Carrey and recent recipients include Julia Roberts , Christopher Nolan, David Fincher and Cate Blanchett .

The first round of voting for the 2027 Césars is Jan.5 with the nominations announced Jan 22. French comedian Vincent Dedienne will host the 52nd César Awards. Léa Seydoux ( Spectre , Blue Is the Warmest Colour ) is acting as chair for the awards and will open the ceremony at L’Olympia cinema in Paris on Feb. 25.

entertainment.title: Quote Of The Day By 'Grey's Anatomy' Star Eric Dane: 'Billie, I'm So Sorry. I'm So Very Sorry That I...'
entertainment.summary: Grey's Anatomy star Eric Dane wrote an apology to his daughter Billie in his memoir, My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments.
entertainment.body:
Although Dane is best known for playing the plastic surgeon in the Shonda Rhimes series, he also had a memorable recurring role in "Charmed" and later starred in "Euphoria," playing Cal Jacobs, Nate's (Jacob Elordi) strict father harboring secrets of his own. Before filming Season 3, Dane was diagnosed with ALS, a fatal neurodegenerative disease. Sam Levinson had to adjust Cal's arc in light of the diagnosis, with the actor appearing a few times in the HBO drama's final season, which aired months after his death.

Aware of his progressive muscle paralysis, Dane did what he could to carry on with his acting career while also spending his remaining days with family. The "Euphoria" star died in February 2026 , only one year after he learned about his condition. Before his death, he recorded an interview for Netflix's "Famous Last Words" and wrote a memoir titled "My Book of Days: A Memoir in Moments," where he could revisit his onscreen legacy and deliver a final message to his loved ones. The quote of the day reflects his continued effort to be present in his daughters' lives, even as he was slowly losing control of his mobility.

TVLine "Billie, I'm so sorry. I'm so very sorry that I can't wrap my arms around you. I wish I could hug you. I can no longer lift my arms."

The quote above comes from Eric Dane's memoir, released on November 3, 2026. In it, the actor revisited moments of his career, his battle with addiction, and the impact of the illness on his relationship with his two daughters, Billie and Georgia.

With little control over his body, Dane solemnly recalls attending Billie's ballet performance of "The Nutcracker" and being unable to wrap his arms around her when she hugged him. Both of them burst into tears, and that made him realize that there were other ways he could express his affection during his physical decline.

"This moment — my daughter holding me, my arms and hands useless, the two of us crying — feels incredibly beautiful, and I think we may be forced to start a new tradition," he added in an excerpt from the book published in People .

Following his diagnosis, Dane learned to approach the disease with "as much grace and dignity" to inspire his daughters to never give up (via TODAY ). His continued struggle to control his muscle movements was hard on him and also hard on his family.

Prior to the memoir's release, his wife Rebecca Gayheart told People that Dane was reluctant to write it. Yet, she's glad he followed through with the memoir, especially because it offers some solace for their children. "It gives my girls the opportunity to know their dad as a human being," she said.

The genre-blurring artist bags the coveted honor for Redstar Wu & The Worldwide Scourge , his third studio album. Dropping in May 2026, Redstar Wu & The Worldwide Scourge debuted at No. 3 on the ARIA Albums Chart — a career best — and topped the Australian Albums Chart and the Vinyl Albums Chart.

Redstar Wu tackles the political, social and economic overwhelm of the last few years, its “soulful, punk-funk electro-rap visionary renders the paranoia and confusion in thrilling, hook-laden tracks that defy neat categorization,” reads a statement from triple j, announcing its annual prize winners. Related Anyma Will Return to the Great Pyramids of Giza In 2027 Ebro & Peter Rosenberg Aren't Buying Ye's 'Comeback' Narrative After Antisemitism: 'It's All Marketing' Yella Beezy Found Guilty in 2020 Murder of Rapper MO3 on a Dallas Highway Explore Genesis Owusu See latest videos, charts and news

The album, however, “doesn’t just rage against dystopia; it optimistically calls to rally people together to overcome forces that tear us apart, offering vigor, hope and imagination in an era where those qualities feel in short supply.”

That’s not all. The Ghana-born, Canberra-raised artist doubles up with the J Award for triple j and rage Australian music video of the year, winning for the clip to “STAMPEDE,” directed by Isaac Brown.

It’s the second time Owusu has won both categories. Previously, he snagged the top award for his debut 2021 album Smiling With No Teeth , and in the same year collected the music video trophy for “The Other Black Dog,” directed by Riley Blakeway.

“We’re incredibly proud to see Genesis Owusu takes home this year’s J Award for album of the year,” comments triple j music director Claire Mooney . “This record is testament to Genesis Owusu’s unmatched and extraordinary creativity, authenticity and ability to create a body of work that is as thought provoking as it is impactful. If there’s one record the world gets to listen to in 2026, I hope it’s this one.”

Since his career erupted with Smiling With No Teeth , Owusu has dominated the awards circuit in Australia like few others. His treasure chest includes the Australian Music Prize, the Vanda & Young Global Songwriting Competition, AIR Awards, and seven ARIAs. He can fill his boots next week at the 2026 ARIA Awards, where he’s nominated in eight categories, equal best on the night with Tame Impala.

entertainment.summary: From the producers of 'Jimmy Savile: A British Horror Story,' the film promises to examine Brand's journey from superstar to convicted rapist.
entertainment.body:
A Russell Brand documentary is coming to Netflix, set to chart his comedy stardom to a criminal trial that culminated in a 10-year prison sentence for rape and sexual assault this week.

Russell Brand: Open Secret is from the producers of Jimmy Savile: A British Horror Story , 72 Films, a Fremantle company, and directed by Olivia Isaacs.

The doc promises to feature inside voices and archive footage, providing insight into Brand’s life and the investigation that started it all at The Times and The Sunday Times , through their chief news correspondent, Rosamund Urwin and investigations correspondent, Charlotte Wace. Crucially, Russell Brand: Open Secret will examine how, despite many people in the TV industry being aware of his behavior, he evaded punishment for so long. Related Stories Movies China's Film Industry Arrives at AFM on a Domestic High Movies Can Constantin Survive Its Own Parent Company?

Brand’s four-week trial at Southwark Crown Court captivated the country and British media. After being sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison on Monday, the disgraced star was led away and transferred to HMP Wandsworth prison. He’ll be expected to serve around seven years of that prison sentence before being released on licence.

The judge, Justice Bennathan, took Brand through all of his crimes in extensive detail, citing the witness impact statements from the four victims before handing down the sentence. He said Brand operated with “staggering arrogance” during the attacks and that his entourage often “indulged” his “dreadful behavior.” He said toward the end of his statement: “Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say ‘no’ and to demand justice from criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent.”

entertainment.title: Netflix to Release Documentary ‘Russell Brand: Open Secret’
entertainment.summary: The film, directed by Olivia Isaacs, centers on the comedian's life and the allegations of sexual offenses that led to his recent trial
entertainment.body:
Netflix will release a new documentary, Russell Brand : Open Secret , on Nov. 13. The film, directed by Olivia Isaacs, “charts the story of Russell Brand’s meteoric rise and steep fall following allegations of sexual offenses.”

According to a press release, Open Secret features inside voices and archive footage that offer insight into Brand’s life and the investigation run by U.K. publications the Times and the Sunday Times and their reporters Rosamund Urwin and Charlotte Wace. A short teaser for the film calls Brand a “shapeshifter” and a “grifter,” and explains that the journalists initially didn’t realize their investigation would lead to criminal charges.

Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault on Nov. 5 following a trial in London. He was found not guilty on two additional counts of rape, as well as one count of attempted indecent assault. The allegations against him were tied to claims made by six women between 1999 and 2009. The actor and comedian was sentenced to 10 years in prison .

Police began investigating Brand in 2023 after multiple women came forward with allegations of assault and abuse in a Channel 4 documentary and the Sunday Times report. Prosecutors first filed five charges against Brand in April 2025, while two additional charges were brought in December.

Following the trial, Brand’s attorney Ian Winter confronted Urwin outside the courtroom, telling her “I hope you are pleased with yourself.” Urwin responded, “I’m pleased justice has been done,” to which Winter replied, “Well, it wasn’t. You fucked it.” Winter later confirmed he had referred himself to the Bar Standards Board.

Urwin explained on a Times podcast that she approached Winter after the verdict because her name had been mentioned during the trial. “I thought he’s talked about me a lot, I’ll go and introduce myself and that is a legitimate thing to do,” she said. “I was surprised to be confronted and spoken to in that way.”

entertainment.title: Arnold Schwarzenegger Calls for Democrats and Republicans to ‘Work Together’
entertainment.summary: "You have to get together and accomplish and be a public servant rather than a party servant"
entertainment.body:
Arnold Schwarzenegger stopped by Jimmy Kimmel Live to promote his new film, The Man With the Bag , and took the opportunity to reflect on being a Republican in today’s political climate.

Kimmel asked the movie star and politician if he is still a Republican early on in their conversation. “Yeah I’m a Republican, absolutely,” Schwarzenegger confirmed, explaining that a “traditional Republican is someone that admires the Republican party for having free the slaves.”

“This is the history,” he explained of the party. “This is what I’m about. Someone that has given those slaves American citizenship and has given them the right to vote is Republican.”

“This sounds like all of the opposite things the Republican party stands for now though, doesn’t it?” Kimmel responded.

“It doesn’t mean I have to change my philosophy,” Schwarzenegger said. “I have my philosophy. The Ronald Reagan philosophy, who created the air resources board in California so we can regulate our own air and reduce our greenhouse gases and pollution in California. That was done by Ronald Reagan, by a Republican. Nixon created the EPA. … So those are the kind of Republicans that used to go and work together with the Democrats and got things done. This is the kind of Republican that I am.”

“Unfortunately I think you’re the only one of them left,” Kimmel noted.

“No, I don’t think I’m the only one left,” Schwarzenegger acknowledged. “But this doesn’t mean that we should give up. The bottom line is we have just seen now what some people call the blue wave. I call it a tidal wave or a tsunami. It’s not really a wave anymore. But the bottom line of that is that now the Democrats go in there and they have the majority. And then the Republicans will go in there and they have the majority. And this is how it goes back and forth and back and forth.”

entertainment.title: ‘12 12 12’ Review: Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan Can’t Save an Apple TV Heist Drama That Lurches From Promising to Disappointing
entertainment.summary: Jim Keeble and Dudi Appleton's eight-episode series uses three interlocking timelines to chronicle the planning, execution and aftermath of a Zurich bank robbery.
entertainment.body:
Logo text For decades, Oreos were a simple thing. Sure, there were versions with a bit more goo or a bit less goo, but the formula was stable because the formula worked.

A handful of years ago, Oreo began innovating, churning out a series of “limited edition” flavors — “limited” because nobody figured that they were ever going to stand on a pedestal with the real thing. Some of those limited edition flavors were pretty good — I dug the BTS-branded “brown sugar pancake” flavor, and I’m a sucker for any of the peanut butter-related experiments — but most have been cloyingly sweet, a few have had no resemblance to the thing they were trying to evoke, and a few have been inedible. Related Stories Movies 'Desert Warrior' Review: Anthony Mackie and Ben Kingsley Star in an Elaborate Slog of a Saudi Epic TV Anthony Mackie Jokes He's the "White Dude Legend" After Multiple Co-Stars Earned Emmy and Oscar Nominations 12 12 12 The Bottom Line A new twist on a genre, but no new inspiration. Airdate: Friday, November 13 (Apple) Cast: Anthony Mackie, Jamie Dornan, Kali Reis, Agathe Rousselle, Sallie Harmsen Creators: Jim Keeble and Dudi Appleton

Like Oreos, the heist genre is a malleable philosophical concept.

If you think about it, the best seasons of Mad Men , The Americans and Better Call Saul all were fundamentally structured as heist stories.

But television has been using its opportunities for longform storytelling to futz around with heist narratives — “Heist Double Stuf,” if you will — for decades, with mostly forgettable results.

You might remember FX’s Thief because Andre Braugher won an Emmy for it or Netflix’s Kaleidoscope for its “watch in any order you want” anarchy, but most recent entries in the genre are more like Hulu’s Culprits , which you probably haven’t even heard of.

Ultimately, it’s very possible that you’ll hear of Apple’s 12 12 12 (especially since if you’re reading this review, you just have). With Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan , it boasts a pair of reasonably well-known stars and, when I get to the part of this review that explains the premise, you’ll probably think the premise has some promise.

The chances of it remaining in any conversation about genre highlights, however, is close to nil. I’ve watched all eight episodes, and the first two illustrate the premise’s potential, the next four illustrate the premise’s limitations, and the last two scrap the premise entirely to deliver an increasingly irritating series of unexciting twists leading to an unsatisfying conclusion.

entertainment.title: Parkway Drive Drives It ‘HOME’ In Career-Defining Concert Film Shot at Sydney Opera House
entertainment.summary: The new documentary traces the Australian rockers on their journey from underdog status in the sweaty metal scene to the stage-and-charts juggernauts they are today.
entertainment.body:
With the rollout this week in cinemas of HOME , Parkway Drive make the rare leap from metalcore to stars of the big screen.

Directed by Allan Hardy ( Viva The Underdogs ) and Macario De Souza ( Bra Boys ), and produced by Hype Republic, the documentary traces the Australian rockers on their journey from underdog status in the sweaty metal scene to the stage-and-charts juggernauts they are today.

Its climax, the band’s one-off live concert at the iconic Sydney Opera House in June 2025, backed by a full symphony orchestra. Related Anyma Will Return to the Great Pyramids of Giza In 2027 Ebro & Peter Rosenberg Aren't Buying Ye's 'Comeback' Narrative After Antisemitism: 'It's All Marketing' Yella Beezy Found Guilty in 2020 Murder of Rapper MO3 on a Dallas Highway Explore Billboard See latest videos, charts and news

Parkway Drive has crashed the Billboard 200, collected No. 1s, ARIA Awards, and played the biggest stages on earth. Few moments, if any, compares to the prospect of playing the Sydney Opera House, capturing the moment for posterity, and pulling it off in the face of potential, ghastly failure.

As far as life experiences go, the concert was somewhere between “wild,” “insane” and “surreal,” frontman Winston McCall tells Billboard over a Zoom.

“Playing the Opera House and everything around this movie has literally been the pinnacle of this man’s career,” he says. “There’s nothing that is ordinary in any way, shape, or form, that will ever be able to be repeated as well, and that can recapture the moment and the work that went into doing what we were doing. And the fact that it was a small fraction of time that so much work went into.”

Hardy and De Souza came to the band with the idea. A suggestion, really. The beginning of a tale, without a middle or an end. “They’re like co-conspirators of ours,” he quips. “They were like, ‘hey, we were in contact with the Opera House, and there’s a date that you guys can play if you want to play. There’s one date available. Do you guys want to do it? You’ve got to say yes, now, basically.’”

The date was six months away, rather close for a band with no plan or idea for the production, and which was, at the time, powering through its 20th anniversary tour.

entertainment.title: ‘Dallas’ star Patrick Duffy recalls night shotgun-wielding teens murdered his parents at Montana bar
entertainment.summary: The “Dallas” actor shared how two teen men returned to his parents’ bar armed with shotguns after his dad kicked them out.
entertainment.body:
Patrick Duffy recalled the horrific night his parents were gunned down at their Montana bar 40 years ago — and how he coped with the devastating loss.

The “Dallas” star, 77, said that two teens armed with shotguns returned to his parents’ bar in Boulder, Mont., after his dad, Terrence, kicked them out earlier that evening for getting drunk and causing trouble on Nov. 18, 1986.

“It was very late at night,” Duffy recalled Monday during an appearance on Steve Kmetko’s “Still Here Hollywood” podcast . “There was nobody in the bar except my father and my mother. And they walked in with their shotguns.”

Terrence saw the 19-year-olds — Sean Wentz and Kenneth A. Miller — return and stepped toward them, telling the pair, “I told you to,” before they opened fire, Duffy said, referencing testimony from his parents’ 1987 murder trial.

Duffy’s mom, Marie, who had been working on a crossword puzzle at the other end of the bar, rushed toward her husband but was also shot and killed.

The gunmen then jumped over the bar, grabbed money from the cash register and stole a couple of bottles of liquor before fleeing.

The bodies of Terrence and Marie were discovered by a group of people who stopped for a drink after a shift change at the Montana Developmental Center, a nearby state institution, according to the Los Angeles Times .

One woman initially thought Marie had fainted when she spotted her on the floor, but noticed blood on Terrence and ran outside to alert a friend.

entertainment.body:
What do you do when the only way to help someone is to break the rules and the law? This clash between compassion and solidarity on the one side and the legal framework on the other is at the heart of A Job Well Done ( Un travail exemplaire ), the new feature blending fiction and documentary from Swiss writer-director Fred Baillif , which dives into the complexities and moral ambiguity that social workers face.

In his work, the former national basketball player and prison educator draws on his background in social work to make films that are rooted in real life and explore contradictions that people working on the tricky frontlines of social services. He previously put a spotlight on street work in Tapis rouge and life in a group home in The Fam ( La Mif ). Related Stories Movies "I Look Good With a Weapon in My Hand": Priyanka Chopra Jonas on Trading Weapons for Words in 'Bluefly' Movies China's Film Industry Arrives at AFM on a Domestic High

In A Job Well Done , Baillif takes us inside a double-decker bus in Geneva, where social workers welcome migrants who are looking for help, a shelter, or simply someone to talk to. On this frontline of Switzerland’s asylum system, the desire to help refugees means navigating an increasingly Kafkaesque bureaucracy.

“Behind every file, a life is told: a young woman in conflict with her family, an asylum seeker facing deportation, homeless people, a woman trying to escape violence,” reads a synopsis on the PÖFF website. “The team looks for solutions, negotiates, insists. But places are scarce, procedures run their course, and institutional responses collide with the urgency of the situations. Among colleagues, convictions clash: keep within the framework to preserve the welcome, or step outside it rather than abandon someone?”

The film will have its world premiere on Nov. 14 in the Official Selection Competition at the the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia. Watch a trailer here.

“What interests me is the moment when a profession collides with bureaucracy without offering real alternatives,” says Baillif. “I want the viewer to experience this conflict.”

A Job Well Done grew out of immersions at AMIC, the Association of Intercultural Mediators, and at the migration and integration center Roseraie in Geneva. Baillif met professionals and the people they support. Through interviews and improvisation workshops, he developed the situations, characters and words from which the screenplay was built with Joanne Giger. The cast brings together professional actors and non-professional performers who know social work or have experience with migration. Through improvisation, the performers find their own words and reactions within a dramaturgical framework.

entertainment.body:
Anyma will return next spring to the Great Pyramids of Giza, Egypt, the setting of his record-setting shows in 2025. Only this time he’s bringing with him one of the great wonders of the electronic music world — Jean-Michel Jarre . Explore Anyma Jean-Michel Jarre See latest videos, charts and news

The Italian-American producer and DJ (real name: Matteo Milleri) will stage two spectacular electronic performances at the Pyramids, titled ÆDEN MILLENNIUM, on March 19 and 26, 2027. “I’m working on a new, entirely unique production for our return in 2027, especially paying tribute to the magnitude of the area’s beauty and history,” he continues. “I can’t wait to share ÆDEN MILLENNIUM with you in Egypt next year.”

Jarre will share the stage for both dates, for what will mark the French electronic music pioneer’s own return to Giza after ringing in the Millennium with his 12-hour production, The Twelve Dreams Of The Sun.

sports.title: Sean McVay laughs as he says he's tempted to ask assistant coach Robert Woods to suit up
sports.summary: He didn't sound completely serious, but Rams coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that he talked to assistant wide receivers coach Robert Woods about whether he could suit up and play while receivers Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington are all out with injuries.
sports.body:
McVay was asked during his press conference whether he has talked to the 34-year-old Woods, who was a receiver for the Rams for five years, about potentially playing again.

McVay acknowledged that there are Collective Bargaining Agreement rules against a coach becoming a player, but he said Woods is still in great shape and it would be fun to give it a try.

“I’ve looked at him, and the way he looks out there, I’ve definitely been tempted,” McVay said. “I think that’d be a violation of the CBA. I don’t know what he’d have to do, but he looks damn good and still is smooth out there. Very tempting.”

Woods was cut by the Steelers before the 2025 season and hasn’t played since, and he announced his retirement and signed a one-day contract with the Rams in February of 2026. Realistically, even with his intimate knowledge of the Rams’ offense, he probably wouldn’t be able to contribute as much on the field as whatever receiver the Rams could add off waivers or another team’s practice squad.

If Woods and the Rams actually wanted him to become an active player, it wouldn’t be as simple as signing him to the active roster, as the league has rules preventing that. Players on the reserve-retired list have to pass through waivers before they can join a team. And the NFL generally doesn’t allow coaches to become players: In 2020, when the Broncos lost all their quarterbacks to covid, they asked the league office if they could activate one of their assistant coaches and were told no. In 2009, Eagles coach Andy Reid wanted to play coaching intern Matt Nagy at quarterback in a preseason game and was also told by the league that he couldn’t.

So the idea of Woods playing receiver for the Rams is probably not going to get any kind of serious consideration. Even if, with all the Rams’ injuries, it’s tempting.

sports.title: For Week 9, Next Gen Stats outpaced the McAfee alt cast again
sports.summary: The ESPN announcement of the viewership for a given Monday night game always requires a careful look for any information about the viewership of the multiple weekly alt casts on the Disney-owned networks.
sports.body:
This week, the release presented only the total viewership for all platforms, at 21.7 million. Nothing was said about the total or individual numbers for the McAfee alt cast on ESPN2 or the Next Gen Stats version on NFL Network.

Andrew Marchand of The Athletic has gotten the numbers . For the Next Gen Stats alt cast, 499,000 tuned in. For the McAfee ensemble, the number was 406,000.

The final tally gives Next Gen Stats a 2-0 lead over the McAfee option. The gap was more narrow this time around; when they first squared off for the Week 6 Commanders-49ers game, NFLN attracted 469,000 and ESPN2 got 351,000 . (ESPN2 is in roughly 70 million homes; NFL Network’s distribution is at or below 50 million.)

The total viewership for that game was 17.9 million. With Bills-Vikings beating that figure by 21.2 percent, Next Gen Stats was up 6.3 percent over Week 6 and the McAfee cast increased by 15.6 percent.

Of the total audience for the game, 2.2 percent watched NFL Network and 1.87 percent watched ESPN2. Which raises, once again, a one-word question: Why?

The Monday night alt casts don’t draw in new viewers. It’s added expense, with no extra revenue for the broader operation. (Unless there’s a tangible benefit to siphoning viewers from ABC/ESPN for the other channels.)

Ultimately, it’s a zero-sum game. With alt casts, Bills-Vikings viewership was 21.7 million. Without alt casts, Bills-Vikings viewership undoubtedly would have been 21.7 million.

And that’s why the various ABC affiliates are upset that Disney will have a full slate of alt casts for Super Bowl LXI. The total number will be the total number, if the game is on one network or twenty. The alt casts will rob the Peter of ABC to pay the Paul of the various other platforms.

Coach Sean McVay said on Wednesday that McDuffie wants to go and the only question for the Rams is whether he’ll be able to do everything he needs to do in a game, which can’t always be simulated on the practice field.

“He’s feeling good. We’re optimistic this week he will be able to go,” McVay said. “He’s so damn tough, but you want to make sure that you’re putting him in a position to have a successful outcome, and he is making really good progress. It’s really just being able to deal with the functional movements and some of the unpredictability.”

Injuries have taken a major toll on the Rams this season, and McDuffie is one of the big-name players in Los Angeles who hasn’t made the impact the team was hoping to see, in large part because he hasn’t been fully healthy. But when asked about McDuffie on Wednesday, McVay answered, “Hopefully this is the week.”

sports.title: Packers-Patriots on Fox leads Week 9 with 25.7 million
sports.summary: As NFL games go, the 4:25 p.m.
sports.body:
That was true on Sunday, when 25.7 million on average tuned in for the window headlined by the Packers shredding the Patriots, 45-27.

It was the most-watched telecast of the week on any network, besting the Bills-Vikings game on Monday night by 4.0 million.

As the NFL is looks for more windows, and potentially heads toward more Wednesday night (and possibly Tuesday night) games, 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday continues to be the best slot.

Currently, that window is shared by CBS and Fox, with one or the other having the game in most weeks. (A few times per year, they both have 4:25 p.m. ET games on the same day.) With all windows (except for Monday night, which is available a year later) opening up in 2030, it will be interesting to see whether the NFL decides to stop splitting all of Sunday afternoon between two networks and selling 4:25 p.m. ET as a weekly package.

Given the audiences generated by that window, it would easily generate the biggest rights fee of any of them.

sports.title: Broncos, Chargers announce Daiyan Henley will not be traded after all
sports.summary: More than 24 hours after the NFL trade deadline, the trade of Henley from the Charges to the Broncos was canceled.
sports.body:
Both the Chargers and the Broncos have announced that Henley will remain with the Chargers. Neither team explained why, but typically that would happen after the trade deadline only if the player failed his physical.

“The proposed trade involving Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley will not be finalized,” the Broncos said in a statement. “We have great respect for Daiyan as a player and person, and we wish him all the best moving forward.”

The Chargers posted “ Welcome back, Daiyan ” on social media, about 30 hours after posting, “Thank you, Daiyan” to officially announce the trade.

According to ESPN, Henley was at the Broncos’ facility on Wednesday and took a physical, so presumably the Broncos’ medical staff decided to nix the trade. Henley did suffer a shoulder injury in Week 8 against the Rams, but he was a full participant in practice the next week and played well in Week 9 against the Texans. There have been no indications that he has had any other health concerns.

The Broncos had agreed to send a 2027 fourth-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Chargers for Henley, who is in the final year of his rookie contract and is slated to become an unrestricted free agent in March.

sports.title: Keenan Allen says his beef with Mike Evans is in the past
sports.summary: Keenan Allen says his beef with Mike Evans is in the past.
sports.body:
Allen joined Evans in the 49ers’ wide receivers room this week after a trade from the Colts.

“We squashed it a long time ago,” Allen said Wednesday, via David Bonilla of 49erswebzone.com. “Everybody wants to bring it back up, obviously. But no, Mike’s a hell of a player. He’s probably better than me at this point.”

In a memorable 2020 back-and-forth on social media , Allen and Evans engaged in a spirited debate about who was the better wide receiver.

Allen was ranked 77th on the NFL Top 100 that season. Tyreek Hill ranked 22nd, Evans 30th and Chris Godwin 38th. Allen argued that he was better than Hill, Evans and Godwin.

“Ok I’m tired of biten my tongue...@cheetah @MikeEvans13_ @chrisgoodwin... ( and the list goes on) ARE NOT a better receiver than me! Faster than me...every day of the week but separation..CHILD PLEASE!” Allen wrote in his post.

Evans responded, “You tagged the wrong Chris Godwin lol and don’t be mad at us we ain’t make the rankings or care about em. I like the confidence but be realistic you not on my level bro.”

Allen, who is in his 14th season, has 1,095 catches for 12,402 yards and 71 touchdowns and is a six-time Pro Bowler. Evans, who is in his 13th season, has 893 catches for 13,472 yards and 111 touchdowns and is a six-time Pro Bowler.

sports.title: Dianna Russini's return includes no specifics about multiple controversies
sports.summary: As expected, Dianna Russini made her return to sports media on Wednesday, with a one-hour show platformed by an illegal offshore sports book.
sports.body:
It’s hardly a prime gig, but her “ crisis publicist ” managed to create plenty of hype — and to finagle a puff piece with People.com that included no questions about the circumstances that prompted Russini’s resignation from The Athletic .

In September, the New York Post reported that Russini would “ share her side of the scandal upon taking her next job.” She hasn’t, and she didn’t in the debut episode of her new show.

Technical difficulties delayed the release of the first episode, which was supposed to be live but seemed to be entirely pre-recorded. (The company blamed the glitch on a “record-breaking audience.” Comparable to what?)

Once the episode finally appeared, it featured three guests (none of whom are current players or coaches), preceded by a segment in which she addressed the future of Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. Which, from an editorial standpoint, is hardly the top story in the NFL on the day after the trade deadline.

There was nothing new or particularly insightful about Jackson. It was a summary of the facts that anyone who has been paying attention to the situation already knew, with a not-groundbreaking assertion that the Ravens want to keep him beyond 2026.

More significantly, the wooly mammoth in the mud room was not addressed. The overriding message was that she went away for a while, she went through some things, and now she’s back. For anyone who doesn’t know the story, she said nothing that would even begin to shed light on it.

If it’s going to be an opinions-and-interviews show, that’s fine. If she’s going to include the reporting of facts about the NFL, the credibility question can’t be ignored.

And this isn’t about the relationship (or whatever it was) with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. It’s about how she responded to it.

sports.title: NC State moves even closer to hiring Philip Rivers
sports.summary: Rivers, who played for the Wolfpack from 1999 through 2003, is now poised to coach them.
sports.body:
Via ESPN, the NC State board of trustees is expected to finalize a contract that will make Rivers the next head coach of the Wolfpack.

Rivers played for NC State from 1999 through 2003. He was the fourth overall pick in the 2004 draft, technically of the Giants. He was traded to the Chargers (with Eli Manning going to New York), and Rivers played for the Chargers through 2019. He spent 2020 with the Colts, and he unexpectedly returned late in the 2025 season to play for the Colts again.

Rivers became a high-school coach in Alabama in 2021. He has never coached at the college or pro level, but he interviewed for the Bills’ head-coaching job.

It’s not known whether he still aspires to coach at the NFL level. As he gets experience at NC State — and if he does well — buzz could build for a shot with an NFL team.

For now, he’ll be returning to the place where he played college football. His name surfaced almost immediately after long-time coach Dave Doeren was fired last month. Along the way, NC State interviewed fellow former NC State quarterback (and NFL quarterback and current CBS analyst) Russell Wilson.

sports.title: Kucherov has natural hat trick in Lightning's 8-3 romp over Sabres

sports.title: Vikings are in the four-quarterback club, for now
sports.summary: The Vikings' addition of quarterback Kirk Cousins comes with a surprising decision on the back end.
sports.body:
Minnesota has not released any of its other quarterbacks. Giving the Vikings four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster.

With Cousins on the team, Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer remain. It’s amazing, frankly, that Wentz hasn’t been cut; Monday night’s performance shows that he should no longer be playing in the NFL. Or the UFL. Or the CFL. Or any organization that ends with “FL.”

It’s hard to imagine Wentz sticking around for long. The Vikings possibly have decided to keep Wentz for now, given that Murray still has a hamstring injury.

Regardless, the soft benching of Murray has now become a hard benching. And the hard benching of Wentz inevitably will become a pink slip.

They’re all in with Cousins. The longer he plays, the better chance the Vikings have to make it to the playoffs.

It starts on Sunday, despite coach Kevin O’Connell being coy about it. Cousins undoubtedly will play. That’s why he’s there.

Even if he’s not 100-percent ready, a less-than-prepared Cousins is better than the other options they have.

sports.title: Kamario Taylor lands $7.5 million deal to return to Mississippi State
sports.summary: One man's chaos is another man's ca-ching.
sports.body:
After years of being stuck in a system that prevented them from getting fair (or any) value for their skills, efforts, and/or sacrifices, college football players are finally getting paid. And one of them is setting a new bar.

Via On3.com, Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor is finalizing a $7.5 million deal to return in 2027. With incentives, it could yield as much as $9 million.

With Taylor under center, the Bulldogs started 4-0. Taylor has since suffered a season-ending injury.

Before the injury, Taylor was regarded as one of the favorites to win the Heisman Trophy.

While the development will prompt the pearl-clutchers to try to parlay the situation into more political momentum for the Protect College Sports Act, it’s a reflection of the free market at work. Which is fine for those in positions of wealth and power, when it comes to their own financial position.

When someone else is reaping the benefits of capitalism in a way that complicates the lives of those who have to balance the books (and to pry cash from boosters who support the NIL funds), it becomes a problem.

And so they’ll do whatever they have to do to roll back the gains players have made. Because free enterprise is desirable only when the people in control practice it.

When the workers start getting paid according to their worth, it becomes a crisis.

sports.title: Bills-Vikings racks up 21.7 million for Monday Night Football
sports.summary: The game itself was not much fun to watch, except for Bills fans.
sports.body:
Via ESPN, 21.7 million watched the Week 9 game between the Bills and Vikings on ABC, ESPN, ESPN2, NFL Network, and ESPN Deportes.

The announcement doesn’t mention the audience for any of the two alt casts — the McAfee gathering on ESPN2 or the Next Gen Stats edition on NFL Network — either individually or collectively.

Next Monday night’s game features the Chargers at the Ravens. It won’t do 21.7 million viewers, primarily since the 0-8 Chargers have become entirely unwatchable.

After that, it’s Bengals-Commanders, Panthers-Buccaneers, Cowboys-Seahawks, Steelers-Jaguars, Patriots-Chiefs, Giants-Lions, and Texans-Packers.

And, yes, the season is already slipping away. Enjoy it while it lasts.

sports.title: Daniel Jones is "not happy" with Colts' roster purge
sports.summary: The Colts had a mini-fire sale in recent weeks, trading away four starters for future assets.
sports.body:
Quarterback Daniel Jones, not surprisingly, isn’t thrilled by the decision to send guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, receiver Keenan Allen, and receiver Josh Downs to other teams.

“I mean, honestly, you’re not you’re not happy to see it, right? ” Jones said. “You’re a player and you’re going out there competing and doing everything you can to win games. So you’re not happy to see a lot of those decisions, and — but like I said, it’s outside of our control, and our job is to play, be prepared, and play well. So, like I said, we got a lot of trust in the guys coming in to those spots, and we’ll be ready to go.”

It’s a bad situation for the players who remain, since it will be harder for them to win with backups thrust into the lineup. But that’s how it works whenever a non-contender admits its situation and trades players.

Those who remain have to keep going, trying to win games even if they get the impression that the front office doesn’t really care.

And even though the Jets hold the Colts’ first-round pick, a bad season for Indianapolis will result in a higher spot in every round. As the Colts embark on a rebuild, it’s not crazy to think the front office hopes to sink as low in the standings as possible, since that will enhance the priority of the picks they have.

The Jets will welcome that, since they have the Colts’ first-round pick. Thanks to the failed trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner.

sports.summary: The Bears have become a significant draw — and it helps when they're in a close game.

Sunday night’s 27-24 win over the Buccaneers generated an audience of 21.5 million for NBC and Peacock.

sports.title: Report: Ravens to sign K Riley Patterson

sports.body:

The Ravens found themselves in need of a new kicker because Jake Moody opted to sign with the Falcons after being elevated from Baltimore’s practice squad in Week 9. Moody became the choice because Tyler Loop is on the team’s injured reserve list.

Patterson opened the season as the Dolphins’ kicker, but was released in October after going 7-of-9 on field goals and 5-of-6 on extra points. He is 97-of-112 on field goals and 148-of-154 on extra points over his entire career.

sports.title: Bills S Amani Hooker: "Amazing" to be on a team that's winning
sports.summary: Safety Amani Hooker was catapulted up the standings this week.
sports.body:
Hooker was traded from Tennessee to Buffalo on Tuesday and the move took him from a 1-7 team to a 7-1 club that has designs on making a long postseason run. Acquiring Hooker to shore up the back end of their defense should help their chances and Hooker said on Wednesday that he was thrilled by the change in circumstances.

“It’s amazing ,” Hooker said, via Nick Suss of ESPN.com. “That’s literally all I can say. Because I’ve been on a team that hasn’t been winning. So I’m obviously very grateful for the Titans and what they did for me. But in the past, we haven’t been winning. And to be on a team that’s putting up points with a quarterback and offensive guys that are on fire, and a great defense, I’m just excited to be here.”

Hooker said he’s confident he will pick up the Bills defense well enough to play against the Jets on Sunday and the process of getting him up to speed will continue over the next couple of days.

sports.title: Browns WR Denzel Boston is expected back at practice Thursday

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills just finished a very tough stretch of their schedule, and they did it while juggling injuries and playing roster-Jenga to keep the right personnel on the game day roster. Now they enter Week 10 as the league’s top team, the AFC’s number one seed and in control of their post-season destiny. sports.title: Christian Mahogany: I need to grow up and stop breaking team rules
sports.summary: Christian Mahogany will return as the Lions' starting left guard on Sunday, a week after his benching for a violation of team rules.
sports.body:
Mahogany apologized to the team Wednesday morning and was back with the first-team offense in the afternoon.

Coach Dan Campbell has said only that Mahogany broke a team rule “multiple times,” but did not elaborate. Mahogany wouldn’t either when he spoke Wednesday.

“I’m not going to [say what the rule was] either. I’m not going to disobey him,” Mahogany said, via Will Burchfield of 97.1 The Ticket. “It sucks what happened, but I have to grow up , and I have to stop breaking team rules. It is what it is. I let my teammates down. I let my organization down, and it won’t ever happen again.”

Campbell’s four team rules are: Don’t be late; keep your weight in check; don’t disrespect your teammates, and don’t disrespect the game. Mahogany first landed in trouble in training camp when he was briefly placed on the non-football injury list.

His absence in Sunday’s win over the Dolphins was noticeable as his replacement, Miles Frazier, had a rough afternoon.

“You just gotta eat it on the chin,” Mahogany said of his benching. “That’s who I am. I’m not a person that’s gonna sulk. It sucked not being out there, because I let my teammates down. I don’t want to do that. I did, and that’s on me.”

sports.title: Meet Ralph: The Sabres' new team dog named in honor of Ralph Wilson

sports.title: 3-5 Panthers face 3-5 Saints for first place in NFC South
sports.summary: It's not often that a matchup of two 3-5 teams carries major playoff implications.
sports.body:
On Sunday in New Orleans, the 3-5 Panthers will take on the 3-5 Saints, and the winner will have sole possession of first place in the NFC South.

The Panthers and Saints are currently tied, with the Panthers in first place thanks to a better division record. Sunday’s winner will be 4-5, a game ahead of the loser and also a game ahead of the 3-6 Buccaneers, who have their bye this week. The 3-6 Falcons face the Chiefs, and the betting odds say Atlanta is likely to fall to 3-7 after that game.

All four teams in the NFC South are bad, but someone has to win the division, and whoever that “someone” is will host a playoff game.

sports.title: Saints RB Travis Etienne has limited practice in his return
sports.summary: Saints running back Travis Etienne returned to practice on Wednesday as a limited participant.
sports.body:
The Saints have 21 days to activate him back to the active roster, but he could return as soon as Sunday.

“We’ll see,” head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday, via Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football. “There’s some potential for it. But . . . we’ll just let the week kind of play out and see what it looks like.”

Etienne has 28 yards rushing, 51 yards receiving and no touchdowns.

Center Erik McCoy (biceps), running back Alvin Kamara (rest/back) and running back C.J. Donaldson (shoulder) did not practice.

Moore said Cesar Ruiz will start at center in McCoy’s absence with Jeremiah Wright taking Ruiz’s spot at right guard.

sports.title: Patrick Mahomes practiced in full on Wednesday: "I'm in a great spot"
sports.summary: While it looked at first on Sunday like Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes had suffered a significant elbow injury, it turns out he hasn't even missed any practice time.
sports.body:
Kansas City listed Mahomes as a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.

Mahomes said in his press conference that he’s in a better spot now, particularly after going through an MRI that did not reveal anything too serious.

"[A]nytime you get in there, you never know what it’s going to show on the machine after,” Mahomes said. “And so, you can feel as optimistic as you do, but then you get in there, and something happens. And so, obviously after talking to the doctors and stuff like that, I feel like I’m in a great spot . Now it’s just about pain and pain management and stuff like that, which I’ll try to do whatever I can to be in the best place possible.”

Mahomes noted he’ll have to do a lot of work in the building and at home to ensure he’s in a good spot for Sunday. But he’s prepared to do so.

“I’ll be able to be out on the practice field, throw the football, and do all that different type of stuff,” Mahomes said. “We’ll continue this process throughout the entire week so I can be 100 percent on Sunday whenever we get to Atlanta. So, it’s a process — a lot more time in the building. But that’s something that I’m willing to do.”

Also on the injury report, right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and defense lineman Peter Woods (neck) did not practice.

Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was limited as he returns from injured reserve.

Cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder), receiver Xavier Worthy (hamstring), receiver Rashee Rice (knee), quarterback Justin Fields (shoulder), linebacker Jeff Bassa (hand), safety Jaden Hicks (shoulder), and tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) were all full.

sports.title: Kirk Cousins plans to talk to Jakobe Thomas about No. 8
sports.summary: Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins made his official return to the team on Wednesday.
sports.body:
Has he spoken to rookie safety Jakobe Thomas, who currently wears No. 8?

“I need to circle back with him,” Cousins told reporters. “Haven’t gotten there. So we’ll have a conversation and I think Mike Parsons will help us, too, in the equipment room. But, yeah, I’ve got to talk to Jakobe for sure.”

When the issue came up again later, Cousins laughed — while also making his intentions clear: “I’m confident that Jakobe and I can have a healthy and mature conversation and figure this out.”

It’s hard to imagine Thomas standing in Cousins’s way. There are too many Vikings fans who still have No. 8 jerseys that will become moot if Cousins isn’t wearing it.

However it goes, it would be a shock if Cousins isn’t wearing No. 8 on Sunday at Lambeau Field.

sports.title: Kevin O'Connell on Kyler Murray: I want him to get healthy, you never know what could happen
sports.summary: The Vikings made Kyler Murray their quarterback choice to open the 2026 season, but it didn't take long for their plans to go awry.
sports.body:
Murray was concussed early in the season opener, missed Week 2 and then led an underwhelming offense to a 4-1 record before suffering a hamstring injury in Week 8. The Vikings offense got even worse with Carson Wentz in Monday night’s loss to the Bills, which led the team to trade for Kirk Cousins on Tuesday.

Head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn’t committed to starting Cousins against the Packers this weekend, but it’s why the deal was made and Murray isn’t currently an option because he remained out of practice with a hamstring injury on Wednesday. Once Murray is healthy, he’ll be slated for a backup role as O’Connell said he doesn’t believe “you can have a competition during the season” and that his hope is that Murray is available if and when the Vikings have to pivot again.

“The reality is what it is ,” O’Connell said. “It’s one of those things where I think he appreciated hearing about it before the transaction took place, but at the same time, he knows I believe in him. I believe in Kyler, just like I believe in Carson and I believe in Max [Brosmer]. I want him to get healthy and get back to work because you just never know. We do not hold the cards in how this will go from a health standpoint or anything like that with anybody on our team.”

O’Connell said that he told Murray that he knows it has been a “less than ideal” series of events, but that underscores the possibility that the Vikings will have to turn back to him with an important game on the line at some point later this year.

sports.body: The Jets recently signed former Steelers defensive lineman Isaiahh Loudermilk to their practice squad. Today, we break him down in detail. The 29-year old Loudermilk is listed at 6’7” and 293 pounds and was a fifth round pick out of Wisconsin in 2021. He has started seven games in his NFL career, with 63 tackles, six passes defensed and one sack. Background Loudermilk was a three-star high school recruit despite only having played 8-man football in a small town. He ended up going to Wisconsin, where he redshirted his first season in 2016, but then became a useful player over the next few years. In 2017, Loudermilk had six tackles in 11 games in a reserve role, adding 1.5 sacks and a pass defensed. He started the first six games of his career in 2018 and ended up with 15 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, three passes defensed and a sack in nine games. In 2019, he started all 14 games and had his most productive season with 24 tackles, five tackles for loss, three sacks, five pass breakups and two forced fumbles. However, Loudermilk got all Big-10 recognition for the only time in his final season as he was named as a third-teamer by the media and an honorable mention by the coaches. In just six games during the pandemic-shortened 2020 season, he had 13 tackles and two sacks. After not being invited to the scouting combine, Loudermilk played in the East-West Shrine Bowl and was eventually drafted by the Steelers in the fifth round of the 2021 draft. As a rookie, he started two games and ended up with 23 tackles, a sack and two pass breakups in 15 appearances. In 2022, Loudermilk started three times but had just seven tackles and a tackle for loss in 11 games overall. He played in 16 games in both 2023 and 2024 but did not start a game during that time. He ended up with 33 tackles, three passes defensed and a quarterback hit over the two seasons. 2025 saw Loudermilk start the first two games, although he didn’t generate any statistics. An injury in the second game sidelined him for the rest of the season. He was almost ready to return for the postseason but wasn’t cleared in time. Loudermilk signed for the Vikings in the offseason but failed to make their roster and was eventually added to the Jets’ practice squad last month. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills didn’t need Josh Allen to put on a superhero cape Monday night. Instead, they leaned on James Cook, a defense that refused to let the Minnesota Vikings find the end zone, and a young tight end who delivered one of the biggest moments of his career. Buffalo’s 23-6 victory over Minnesota was a team effort, and head coach Joe Brady’s postgame Game Balls reflected exactly that. It wasn’t necessarily the flashiest performance of his career, averaging 3.5 yards per carry, but it was exactly what Buffalo needed. His five-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter capped a 15-play, 84-yard drive that drained 8:32 off the clock and effectively put the game out of reach. Brady also recognized Cook for reaching the 5,000-career-rushing-yard milestone, another significant accomplishment for Buffalo’s running back. The milestone adds to a night when Cook carried the offense, helping the Bills dominate time of possession and secure their second consecutive victory. Cook continues to prove he can be more than an explosive-play threat. When the Bills need to grind out yards, extend possessions, and keep their defense fresh, he’s more than capable of carrying the workload. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills didn’t need an offensive explosion to take care of business on Monday Night Football. Instead, they controlled the clock, leaned heavily on James Cook, and delivered one of their most complete defensive performances of the season in a 23-6 win over the Minnesota Vikings. Buffalo held the ball for an incredible 42:32, leaving Minnesota’s offense on the field for just 17:28. The Bills ran 80 offensive snaps compared to only 48 defensive snaps, a significant workload difference that tells much of the story. Minnesota finished with just 178 total yards, nine first downs, an 0-for-8 performance on third down, and failed on both fourth-down attempts. The Vikings also committed three turnovers. Offense: 80 snaps James Cook played 51 offensive snaps (64%), finishing with 31 carries for 107 yards and a touchdown. That’s a substantial workload, particularly considering Buffalo ran the ball 44 times. Cook averaged just 3.5 yards per carry, but his production wasn’t about explosive plays. It was about keeping the offense moving, wearing down Minnesota’s defense, and helping Buffalo control the clock. Ty Johnson played 17 snaps (21%), while Ray Davis saw 11 (14%). Johnson contributed a 36-yard reception on third-and-eight, Buffalo’s longest offensive play of the night. The distribution is interesting because Cook accounted for 31 of Buffalo’s 44 rushing attempts despite playing just 64% of the offensive snaps. When Cook was on the field, the Bills clearly wanted the ball in his hands. Kincaid contributed three receptions for 28 yards, while Hawes added an eight-yard reception.. The continued use of four tight ends is worth watching. sports.body: A year after making a pair of franchise-altering deals at the NFL trade deadline, the Jets stayed quiet this year. The only trade they made was a minor one, sending backup safety Andre Cisco to the Detroit Lions in exchange for a future sixth round pick. The Jets did not trade defensive end Will McDonald despite McDonald requesting a deal to a new team and other teams reportedly having interest. [Media: https://twitter.com/Schultz_Report/status/2119841495251624248] It probably shouldn’t be a massive surprise to see the Jets stay out of the trade market. At 2-7, there would be no way to justify this team being a buyer. At the same time, a coaching staff and possibly front office fighting for its respective jobs might not be willing to give up quality players in exchange for future Draft picks they might not be around to make. So we ended up with a trade deadline that lacked much activity for this team.

sports.body: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. Buffalo Bills president of football operations/general manager Brandon Beane did it again, tackling one of the team’s biggest roster needs just hours before the 2026 NFL trade deadline. The Bills have reportedly made a trade to bring in 28-year-old safety Amani Hooker, previously of the Tennessee Titans. It represents a move that most of Bills Mafia have been banging the folding tables for going on weeks now, due to the often confused assignments and play observed out of Buffalo’s defensive secondary. The deal for Hooker also reveals another savvy move by Beane to leverage all layers of quality in negotiating a trade. Specifically, Buffalo sent a 2027 second-round pick to the Titans in return for Hooker and a fifth-round pick. One Bills Drive was also rumored to have been looking into making a trade for safety Budda Baker of the Arizona Cardinals, but Arizona’s front office relented. Many Bills fans were concerned when they found out Buffalo hadn’t pulled off a trade with the Atlanta Falcons to land safety Jessie Bates, instead watching him head to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Despite that concern, it’s now clear that Beane was working the phones to improve the Bills’ roster, and it’s a deal that looks better on paper compared to what Jacksonville gave up to get Bates. Hooker is younger than Bates, and he’s a player who gives the Bills more roster control at the position while spending less capital to acquire him, as outlined by Matt Warren. Hooker currently leads the NFL with five interceptions, three of which came in one game against quarterback Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals. sports.body: Let’s break down some of the financial and draft-pick implications of the Buffalo Bills trading for veteran safety Amani Hooker before the NFL trade deadline. Hooker is a 28 year old in his eighth professional season, all of which, until now, were spent with the Tennessee Titans, the club that selected him in the fourth round out of the University of Iowa in 2019. Draft-pick value for Bills to acquire Amani Hooker On the Jimmy Johnson trade value chart — using the NFL draft order after Week 9’s action — the Bills paid the equivalent of between the No. 71 and No. 72 overall pick (Round 3) to acquire Hooker. How many picks do the Bills now have in the 2027 NFL Draft? After the Hooker trade, the Bills have nine picks in the 2027 NFL Draft: Round 1 - Own Round 3 - Own Round 4 - Own Round 4 - Expected compensatory selection for David Edwards’ departure Round 5 - Titans from Amani Hooker trade Round 5 - Own Round 6 - Colts from Sedrick Van Pran-Granger trade Round 6 - Own Round 7 - Raiders How long is Amani Hooker signed? Hooker is currently signed through the 2028 season. He has a prorated salary of $4.47M for the 2026 season. According ESPN NFL reporter Cameron Wolfe, the Titans are not eating any of Hooker’s remaining 2026 salary. Hooker is set count $10.28M in 2027 and $13.5M in 2028. Of course, the Bills can redo Hooker’s deal if the two sides can agree on terms, but for a team that is currently allocating the third-fewest amount of money to the safety position — and is currently set to allocate the seventh-lowest in 2027 and 12th-lowest to that position in 2028 — Hooker’s future cap hits are very manageable. Does Amani Hooker have any connections to any Bills players? Yes. Hooker and Bills practice-squad safety Geno Stone were teammates at Iowa in 2017 and 2018.

sports.body: This season has gone completely off the rails for the New York Jets. One of the few silver linings is that the team is set to have multiple high first round picks. The Jets’ own pick will be high given the team’s struggles, and both the Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys are having difficult seasons. If the season ended today, the Jets would be sitting on three picks in the top 13 of the 2027 NFL Draft. - Chargers 0-8 - Titans 1-7 - Dolphins 1-7 - Jets (from Colts 2-7) - Eagles 2-7 - Jets 2-7 - Commanders 2-5-1 - Buccaneers 3-6 - Cardinals 3-6 - Falcons 3-6 - Texans 3-5 - Saints 3-5 - Jets (from Cowboys 3-5) - Ravens 4-5 - Raiders 4-5 - Browns 5-4 - Seahawks 5-4 - Browns (from Rams 5-4) Picks 19 through 32 are determined by the results of NFL Playoff games. Once again Jets fans are focused on the NFL Draft in November as another season has resulted in failure. At least this year the NFL Draft should be very exciting.
